title: The rich man and Lazarus: their opposite fates
english: There was a rich man who rejoiced daily in splendor, and a poor man named Lazarus had been laid at his gate, covered with sores, according to the gospel story. It happened, then, that both died, and the poor man departed into rest, but the other into punishment (Luke 16:19-22).

added_allusions.reason: Recorded (justifications/frag-open.json, method: wording). The Greek Anthropos tis en plousios (there was a rich man), ptokhos de tis Lazaros (a poor man named Lazarus), helkomenos (covered with sores), and the death of both reproduce Luke 16:19-22. The justification's note mentions the bosom of Abraham, but the locked source reads eis ten anapausin (into rest); the entry stands on Luke 16:19, Luke 16:20, and the death, not on that phrase.

translator_notes: True OET from PG 77 / Vat. gr. 447 Greek; Pass A ≠ Pass B.
Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify; skip Pusey-PD / Greystone / Lunn / Hill.
orientation: Cyril opens his treatise by summarizing the gospel story of the rich man and Lazarus and their opposite fates after death.
